subject: History
description: Covers the First to Fourth Councils, patrons, and outcomes.

questions.stem: The First Buddhist Council was convened immediately after the Mahaparinirvana (death) of Lord Buddha. Where was it held and under whose patronage?

options.option_text: Rajagriha, under the patronage of King Ajatashatru
Vaishali, under the patronage of King Kalashoka
Pataliputra, under the patronage of Emperor Ashoka
Kashmir, under the patronage of King Kanishka

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The First Buddhist Council was held in 483 BC in the Sattapanni caves at Rajagriha (modern Rajgir, Bihar). It was patronized by King Ajatashatru of the Haryanka dynasty. It was presided over by the monk Mahakashyapa. The core objective was to preserve the Buddha's teachings. Here, the Sutta Pitaka (Buddha's discourses) was recited by Ananda, and the Vinaya Pitaka (rules of monastic discipline) was recited by Upali.
DECOY BUSTING: The other options represent the Second, Third, and Fourth councils respectively. This is a very common chronological sequence to memorize for exams: R-V-P-K (Rajagriha, Vaishali, Pataliputra, Kashmir).
EXAM INSIGHT: Understanding the outcome of each council is vital. The First compiled the Pitakas. The Second saw the first major split (Sthaviras and Mahasanghikas). The Third compiled the Abhidhamma Pitaka. The Fourth saw the formal split into Hinayana and Mahayana.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The great schism of Buddhism into the Hinayana (Lesser Vehicle) and Mahayana (Great Vehicle) sects officially occurred during which Buddhist Council?

options.option_text: Fourth Buddhist Council
Third Buddhist Council
Second Buddhist Council
First Buddhist Council

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir (or Jalandhar) in the 1st century AD under the patronage of the Kushan emperor Kanishka. It was presided over by Vasumitra. It was at this council that Buddhism officially split into two major distinct sects: Mahayana (which believed in the divinity of Buddha and idol worship) and Hinayana (which adhered to the original, orthodox teachings of Buddha as a mortal teacher).
DECOY BUSTING: The Second Council saw an earlier, minor disciplinary split, but the formal doctrinal split into Mahayana and Hinayana was strictly at the Fourth Council. The Third Council (under Ashoka) was an attempt to resolve disputes and rid the Sangha of corruption.
EXAM INSIGHT: The Mahayana sect spread rapidly to Central Asia, China, Japan, and Korea, largely driven by the missionary zeal of Kanishka and the appeal of Bodhisattvas (saviors). Hinayana (Theravada) became dominant in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Which Mauryan Emperor patronized the Third Buddhist Council, and what was its major literary achievement?

options.option_text: Ashoka; the compilation of the Abhidhamma Pitaka
Chandragupta Maurya; the writing of the Jataka tales
Bindusara; the translation of the Tripitaka into Sanskrit
Brihadratha; the creation of the Milinda Panha

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Third Buddhist Council was convened in 250 BC at Pataliputra (Patna) under the patronage of Emperor Ashoka the Great. It was presided over by the monk Moggaliputta Tissa. The council's major literary achievement was the compilation of the Abhidhamma Pitaka, which forms the third part of the Pali Tripitaka and deals with the deep philosophical and psychological analysis of the Buddha's teachings.
DECOY BUSTING: Chandragupta Maurya converted to Jainism, not Buddhism. Bindusara supported the Ajivika sect. The Jatakas and Milinda Panha were composed independently over time.
EXAM INSIGHT: Ashoka convened this council to purify the Buddhist Sangha of opportunistic monks who had joined solely to enjoy royal patronage. After this council, Ashoka sent Buddhist missionaries to various parts of the world, including sending his son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Second Buddhist Council was convened approximately a century after Buddha's death to address disciplinary disputes. At which city was it held?

options.option_text: Rajagriha, the capital of ancient Magadha kingdom
Vaishali, located in present-day Bihar state
Pataliputra, where Ashoka later held his council
Sravasti, the city of Jetavana monastery fame

questions.explanation: The Second Buddhist Council (c. 383 BCE) was held at Vaishali. Rajagriha hosted the First Council; Pataliputra hosted the Third Council under Ashoka. Vaishali was chosen because the Vajjian monks whose practices triggered the council were based there.

questions.stem: Which elder monk presided over the First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha, and what was his specific role in organizing it?

options.option_text: Ananda, who recited the Sutta Pitaka at the council
Upali, who was entrusted to recite the Vinaya Pitaka
Mahakassapa, who convened and presided over the assembly
Sariputta, foremost among disciples in wisdom

questions.explanation: Mahakassapa (Maha Kasyapa) presided over the First Council at Rajagriha. Ananda recited the Suttas and Upali recited the Vinaya — they participated but did not preside. Sariputta is a deliberate trap: he predeceased the Buddha and could not have been present at the council.

questions.stem: Unlike later Buddhist councils that centred on doctrinal disagreements, the Second Council at Vaishali was fundamentally a dispute over what type of issue?

options.option_text: Canonical status of the Abhidhamma Pitaka collection
Ten proposed relaxations of Vinaya monastic discipline
Buddha's divine versus purely human ontological nature
The correct liturgical language for reciting scriptures

questions.explanation: The Second Council debated the 'Dasavatthuni' (Ten Points) — relaxations of Vinaya rules practiced by Vajjian monks, including accepting gold and silver. The council ruled these unlawful. The divine-versus-human nature of the Buddha became a doctrinal issue only after the Mahasanghika schism that followed.

questions.stem: The Fourth Buddhist Council convened under Kushan emperor Kanishka in Kashmir was a major Sarvastivada assembly. Who is traditionally identified as its president (chairman)?

options.option_text: Nagasena, the monk famous for Milindapanha dialogues
Vasumitra, the Sarvastivada scholar appointed to chair it
Nagarjuna, the founder of the Madhyamaka philosophical school
Buddhaghosa, the fifth-century Pali Canon commentator

questions.explanation: Vasumitra presided over Kanishka's Fourth Council (held at Kundalavana, Kashmir, c. 1st–2nd century CE). Nagasena is associated with the Milindapanha, a much earlier text; Nagarjuna founded Madhyamaka philosophy but did not chair this council; Buddhaghosa (5th century CE) postdates the council entirely.

questions.stem: The Buddhist Council held under Kanishka produced a major Sarvastivada commentary that systematised Abhidharma teachings across seven canonical texts. What is this voluminous work called?

options.option_text: Kathavatthu — Moggaliputta Tissa's doctrinal disputation text
Dipavamsa — the early Pali chronicle of Buddhism in Lanka
Mahavibhasha — the great Sarvastivada Abhidharma commentary
Milindapanha — philosophical dialogue of Nagasena with King Milinda

questions.explanation: The Mahavibhasha ('Great Commentary') was the principal achievement of Kanishka's council, systematising Sarvastivada Abhidharma. Kathavatthu belongs to Ashoka's Third Council; Dipavamsa is a Sri Lankan chronicle unrelated to Kanishka's council; Milindapanha predates the council and was composed independently.

questions.stem: The Theravada tradition recognises a distinct Fourth Council held in Sri Lanka around 29 BCE under King Vattagamani Abhaya at Aluvihara. What was its historically unique and consequential achievement?

options.option_text: Committing the complete Pali Tipitaka to writing on palm-leaf manuscripts
Revising Vinaya codes to formally condemn Mahasanghika practices
Dispatching missionary monks to Myanmar and mainland Southeast Asia
Composing Milindapanha as a written rebuttal to Greek philosophy

questions.explanation: The Aluvihara council (c. 29 BCE) marks the first instance in Buddhist history of the oral Tipitaka being written down on palm leaves — prompted by famine and warfare that threatened the survival of trained oral reciters. Missionary dispatch was an outcome of Ashoka's Third Council; Milindapanha was an independent composition, not a council product.

questions.stem: After the Second Buddhist Council, the Mahasanghikas developed a distinctive doctrinal position on the nature of the Buddha that sowed the seeds of later Mahayana theology. Which of the following correctly identifies that position?

options.option_text: They denied that the historical Buddha achieved final Nirvana at death
They asserted the Buddha's physical form was a magical illusion body
They argued the Buddha personally dictated every Sutta to Ananda
They held the Buddha possessed a wholly supramundane (lokottara) nature

questions.explanation: The Mahasanghikas' 'lokottaravada' — the doctrine that the Buddha was wholly supramundane (lokottara), beyond all human limitation — directly prefigured the Mahayana concept of an omniscient transcendent Buddha. Option A conflates with later Mahayana Nirvana theology; option B (illusory body) is closer to the full Trikaya doctrine that emerged much later in Mahayana development.
